version.author: kallums
version.changelog: First release. A catalogue of musical ideas generated for your scale, your chords and the instrument you are writing for. Rhythm (ostinato, pulse, syncopation, gallop, tresillo, hemiola, polyrhythm, arpeggio, repeated note, Alberti, broken chord), melody (ascending, descending, arch, wave, sequence, call and response, repetition, development) and harmony (triadic, quartal, cluster, pedal, arpeggiated, contrary motion), for 25 orchestral instruments and four sections. Every entry is calculated, never random, and checked for the instrument's range, speed at your tempo, leaps and breathing, and for the harmony. Transform, repeat and accent it, then insert it at the edit cursor (a section gets a track per instrument), export a .mid, or audition it. Needs ReaImGui.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: Chain your own chords. The chords are now a row you build, up to eight: any of Starting Blocks' 78 named chords (7ths, extended, altered, sus and add, quartal, Tristan, So What and more) or the 9 the scale builds, on any degree. Click a chord to change it, + to add one, - to remove one, or start again from a common progression. Under a chord with notes your scale lacks - a borrowed C major in C minor, a D7 in C major - everything in the catalogue plays the chord's own notes. A smaller window: instruments show a family at a time with the register beside them, and the chord editor opens only while you are changing a chord.
